title: Conflict between texts — reading-desk microscene
titleEs: Conflicto entre textos — Microescena con objetos y actores
description: Top-down reading desk: an assistant slides a fictional article towards an open book until their provisions face each other; both tension phrases are highlighted, the zone of tension is drawn across the seam, the reader inspects it with a lens and the assistant sets the supplied marker (pennant pin, paper clip or none). An editable hierarchy board shows a user-supplied ordering that is never applied; no text is shown to prevail.

content.note: Visual illustration only. It does not state the law of any jurisdiction or decide validity, responsibility or outcomes.

license: Original vector artwork and code created for this project; no third-party assets.

durationMs.description: Total length of the finite timeline in milliseconds. Phases scale proportionally; the final state is held.

seed.description: Seed for small deterministic variations (appearance defaults, hand-drawn jitter). Same seed + time + params = same frame.

locale.description: Language of built-in labels (en or es). User-supplied text is never translated.

theme.description: Render treatment. Only tested themes are listed.

palette.description: Colour palette applied to props, actors and accents.

background.description: transparent, paper, white, light-grey, charcoal or a #rrggbb colour.

safeArea.description: Caption-safe margins as fractions of the frame.

reducedMotion.description: Removes decorative motion (overshoot, idle sway, camera drift) while keeping instructional motion.

textVisibility.description: all labels, key labels only, or none (the action must remain readable without labels).

jurisdiction.description: Descriptive jurisdiction tag. "unspecified" means no legal system is asserted.

contentNotice.description: Shows a small "illustrative example" tag inside the safe area.

id.description: Short identifier printed on the index tab and on its hierarchy token

provision.description: Provision reference printed above its passage (fictional)

sources.description: The two fictional texts brought together: the first is the book (anchor), the second the article (array replaces the previous value)

levels.description: Level labels, top to bottom (user-supplied, neutral) (array replaces the previous value)

placement.description: Level of each text (0 = first level), same order as sources; values beyond the last level use the last level (array replaces the previous value)

caption.description: Caption printed at the foot of the board

hierarchy.description: Editable hierarchy: a user-supplied ordering of the two texts shown on a slotted board. Neutral labels by default; it is displayed, never applied as an ordering rule and never used to resolve the conflict

tension.description: Phrase of that wording highlighted as the zone of tension; if it does not occur in the wording it is shown as a separate marked line

passages.description: Simulated wording of each provision (same order as sources) and the phrase highlighted as its zone of tension (array replaces the previous value)

by.description: Fictional source the reading is attributed to

text.description: Reading as proposed by that source

interpretations.description: Readings attributed to fictional sources; shown as attributed notes ("reading proposed"), never endorsed (array replaces the previous value)

a.description: Caption for the reader (the hand that brings the lens)

b.description: Caption for the assistant (the hand that slides the article and places the marker)

actorLabels.description: Role captions shown next to each actor

hierarchy.description: Heading printed on the editable hierarchy board

actionProgress.description: How far the concrete action is allowed to progress (1 = complete; lower values freeze it part-way)

target.description: Scene element the annotation points at

items.description: Editorial annotation shown during the hold

annotations.description: Editorial callouts shown in the final hold (array replaces the previous value)

finalState.description: State supplied by the author for the zone of tension in the final hold: conflict-flagged (pennant pin), compatible-application (paper clip) or tension-highlighted (no marker). Nothing is inferred and no text is shown to prevail
